detailed_sections.section_number_and_title: 4.1 Law, Substantive Justice, and Procedural Justice
detailed_sections.full_notes: Laws are rules enforced by the state. Substantive justice ensures the outcome is fair, reasonable, and equitable. Procedural justice guarantees every person a fair hearing, legal representation, and presumption of innocence until proven guilty.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: 2023 Criminal Law Overhaul
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (replacing IPC 1860), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (replacing CrPC 1973), and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (replacing Evidence Act 1872).

detailed_sections.section_number_and_title: 4.2 Court Hierarchy and Alternative Dispute Resolution
detailed_sections.full_notes: India has an integrated judicial hierarchy: Supreme Court -> High Courts -> Subordinate District Courts. To reduce backlog, Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) modes like Lok Adalats, Mediation (Mediation Act 2023), and Gram Nyayalayas provide affordable, speedy justice.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: First PIL Landmark Case
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Kapila Hingorani filed a writ petition securing the release of 40,000 undertrial prisoners in Bihar who had been detained longer than their maximum potential sentence.
